reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.

consistencyRules.message: The +1 modifier applies to continuous cord compression in the setting of a neurological deficit.

commonErrors: Scoring several morphologies instead of the most severe.
Applying the +1 modifier without a deficit.
name: Subaxial Cervical Spine Injury Classification (SLIC)

version.label: SLIC (Vaccaro et al. 2007)
version.detail: Morphology 0–4 + discoligamentous complex 0–2 + neurological status 0–3, plus 1 for continuous cord compression with a neurological deficit. Total 0–10.

purpose: Classifies subaxial (C3–C7) cervical spine injuries and summarises features relevant to management.
intendedPopulation: Adults with subaxial cervical spine trauma, using CT, MRI and neurological examination.

calculatorNotice.title: Classification, not a surgical decision
calculatorNotice.message: The authors proposed treatment thresholds; management also depends on the patient, associated injuries and surgeon judgement.

inputDefinitions.label: Morphology

options.label: Compression (including endplate or vertical body fracture)
Rotation or translation (e.g. facet dislocation, unstable teardrop)

inputDefinitions.help: Score the most severe morphology at the level.

options.label: Indeterminate (e.g. isolated interspinous widening, MRI signal change only)
Disrupted (e.g. widened disc space, facet perch or dislocation)

inputDefinitions.label: Continuous cord compression with a neurological deficit

resultStates.label: SLIC 4
resultStates.summary: Score 4: indeterminate in the authors' scheme.
resultStates.detail: Management depends on patient and injury factors.

resultStates.label: SLIC {total}
resultStates.summary: Score 5 or more: the authors' operative range.
resultStates.detail: Management depends on neurological status, associated injuries, patient factors and surgical judgement.

clinicalContext.text: Combines injury morphology, ligamentous integrity and neurology, the three features that drive management.

clinicalInsights.text: Incomplete cord injury scores higher than complete because decompression may improve it.

limitations.text: Proposed thresholds are not a substitute for surgical judgement.

limitations: DLC assessment on MRI is variably interpreted.

guideSections.what: A 0–10 score from morphology, discoligamentous complex and neurology for C3–C7 injuries.
guideSections.howToPerform: Score the most severe morphology, the DLC and the neurological status; add 1 for continuous cord compression with a deficit.
guideSections.clinicalContext: A classification that supports management decisions made with the full clinical picture.

sources.citation: Vaccaro AR, Hulbert RJ, Patel AA, et al. The subaxial cervical spine injury classification system: a novel approach to recognize the importance of morphology, neurology, and integrity of the disco-ligamentous complex. Spine. 2007;32(21):2365-2374.

components.label: Continuous cord compression with a neurological deficit
